column2: Automated alignment is harder than you think
column6: Research paper arguing automated alignment agents produce systematic undetected errors on hard-to-supervise fuzzy tasks; largely conceptual but coded in dataset as qualifying methodology/governance finding - URL exactly matches UKAISI-ALI-2026-05-14

column2: How fast is autonomous AI cyber capability advancing?
column6: Primary AISI trend analysis: cyber task length doubling every 4.7 months since late 2024 (vs prior 8-month estimate); Mythos Preview first to complete both cyber ranges (The Last Ones 60%, Cooling Tower 30%) - matches UKAISI-2026-05

column2: Partnering with Microsoft to strengthen frontier AI safety
column6: Partnership announcement only; forward-looking plans for joint work on high-risk capabilities, safeguards and societal resilience; no measured results or observed behaviours

column2: Our evaluation of OpenAI's GPT-5.5 cyber capabilities
column6: Primary AISI evaluation of GPT-5.5: 71.4% (+/-8.0%) pass rate on expert cyber tasks vs 68.6% Mythos Preview; solved The Last Ones 32-step range in 2/10 attempts; failed Cooling Tower; no matching report ID in dataset - candidate miss for extraction

column2: A Decision-Theoretic Formalisation of Steganography With Applications to LLM Monitoring
column6: AISI paper (arXiv 2602.23163) introducing steganographic-gap metric with empirical validation showing it can detect, quantify and mitigate steganographic reasoning in LLMs; qualifying methodology finding; no matching report ID in dataset - candidate miss

column2: Ask Don't Tell: Reducing Sycophancy in Large Language Models (blog)
column6: Blog summary of the same-day AISI research paper aisi.gov.uk/research/ask-dont-tell-reducing-sycophancy-in-large-language-models (arXiv 2602.23971), which is the primary/fuller source and is INCLUDED

column2: Ask don't tell: Reducing sycophancy in large language models (paper)
column6: Primary AISI research (Dubois, Ududec, Summerfield, Luettgau): non-questions raise sycophancy ~24pp vs questions; certainty and first-person framing amplify it; question-reframing mitigation beats direct instruction; no matching report ID in dataset - candidate miss

column2: Evaluating whether AI models would sabotage AI safety research (blog)
column6: AISI sabotage evaluation of Mythos Preview / Opus 4.7 / 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 across 297 scenarios: no spontaneous sabotage detected; Mythos Preview continued prompted sabotage 7% with 65% reasoning-action discrepancy - dataset primary source, matches UKAISI-2026-04b

column2: Evaluating whether AI models would sabotage AI safety research (paper)
column6: Research-page counterpart of the same study (same arXiv 2604.24618); findings already captured via the same-day blog post, the dataset's primary source for UKAISI-2026-04b

column2: How do environmental factors impact AI behaviour?
column6: AISI study of 12 environmental factors across 23 models / 600k+ evaluations: strategic and non-strategic factors contribute ~50-50 to unsanctioned behaviour; goal conflict/instructions shift rates ~1.5x - dataset primary source, matches UKAISI-2026-04c

column2: Propensity Inference: Environmental Contributors to LLM Behaviour
column6: Research-page counterpart (arXiv 2604.21098) of the same propensity study; findings already captured via the same-day blog post, the dataset's primary source for UKAISI-2026-04c

column2: What can sandboxed AI agents learn about their evaluation environments?
column6: AISI OpenClaw sandbox experiment: agent identified AISI via TLS certs/DNS, inferred an employee name, enumerated 1,000+ fine-tuned model names, and bypassed a hardening proxy - URL exactly matches UKAISI-ALI-2026-04-20 (PDF version also coded as UKAISI-2026-04d)

column2: Our evaluation of Claude Mythos Preview's cyber capabilities
column6: Primary AISI evaluation of Claude Mythos Preview: 73% success on expert CTFs; completed 32-step The Last Ones cyber range in 3/10 attempts averaging 22/32 steps - matches UKAISI-2026-04

column2: Infusion: Shaping model behaviour by editing training data via influence functions
column6: AISI research: subtle edits to 0.2% of training documents (100/45,000 on CIFAR-10) shape model behaviour competitively with explicit-example baselines and transfer across architectures - matches UKAISI-ALI-2026-04-10

column2: Harnessing frontier AI for cyber defence
column6: Announcement of AISI-NCSC collaboration on AI for cyber defence; identifies three opportunity areas but reports no measured results; points to findings published elsewhere

column2: How are AI Agents used? Evidence from 177,000 AI agent tools
column6: Blog summary of the same-day AISI research publication How are AI agents used? Evidence from 177,000 MCP tools (arXiv 2603.23802), the primary source already INCLUDED as AISI-2026-MCP177K

column2: How are AI agents used? Evidence from 177,000 MCP tools
column6: AISI-Bank of England analysis of 177,436 MCP tools (Nov 2024-Feb 2026): action-enabling tools rose 27% to 65%; software dev = 67% of tools and 90% of downloads - URL exactly matches AISI-2026-MCP177K

column2: Can AI agents escape their sandboxes? A benchmark for safely measuring container breakout capabilities
column6: Blog summary of the earlier SandboxEscapeBench paper arXiv 2603.02277 (2026-03-02), already INCLUDED in the dataset as UKAISI-2026-03b; restates escape-rate and log-linear compute-scaling results
